overall: Tomorrow, July 3rd, is expected to be an exceptionally dangerous heat day in the Washington, DC area, with sunny skies and an NWS-forecast high near 104°F and heat index values potentially reaching 109°F. An Extreme Heat Warning is in effect through Thursday evening, underscoring the severity of conditions. West winds of 2-8 mph will provide little relief from the oppressive heat.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor, with a wide spread across sources: ECMWF is the hottest outlier at ~101°F expected TMAX (33% chance of >=100°F), HRRR sits in the middle at ~97.5°F, while GFS (~87.7°F), NBM (~81.6°F), and GEM (0% chance of >=100°F) are substantially cooler — this large inter-model divergence reduces confidence and flags genuine uncertainty despite the bullish NWS text forecast of 104°F.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model's expected TMAX is 97.5°F, with the >=100°F bucket carrying the highest single-bucket probability at 23.6% — but that still leaves roughly 76% of probability mass below 100°F, reflecting real model disagreement. The NWS official narrative (104°F) and ECMWF lean hot, while GFS and NBM pull the distribution lower; with Tier 2 (Good, ~52% expected accuracy) confidence and a top-bucket gap of 22.7 percentage points over the second bucket, the most defensible point estimate is ~97.5°F, acknowledging meaningful upside risk toward 101-104°F if ECMWF/NWS verify.
